```{r setup, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
has_mgcv <- requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE)
options(width = 76)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%", dpi = 96,
                      eval = has_mgcv)
# Cut each figure to a palette of 256 colours, about a third of its size with
# no visible change, because the built vignettes ship in the tarball
if (requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.process = function(path) {
    img <- magick::image_quantize(magick::image_read(path), max = 256,
                                  colorspace = "sRGB", dither = FALSE)
    magick::image_write(img, path, format = "png")
    path
  })
}
# Write a share as a percentage to one decimal for the prose
percent <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
```

```{r no-mgcv, eval = !get0("has_mgcv", ifnotfound = TRUE), echo = FALSE, results = "asis", purl = FALSE}
cat(paste0(
  "**The code on this page was not run when the page was built, because mgcv is not ",
  "installed, so the page shows no results or figures.** Install it with ",
  "`install.packages(\"mgcv\")`, then run the page's script, ",
  "`system.file(\"scripts\", \"range-model.R\", package = \"detfield\")`.\n"
))
```

**detfield** never fits a range model. `de_model()` takes the one you fitted: a `glm`, an
**mgcv** `gam` or a **glmmTMB** model, a table of curve values, or a function of distance and
depth. Fit a smooth over time with **mgcv**: `de_model()` drops random effects, so the `s()`
smooth of a **glmmTMB** model reaches the field as a straight line.
`de_logistic()` builds a curve from two distances, for a study with no range test. Detection
range varies across a water body and over time, with receiver depth, wind, noise, temperature
structure and the bottom, and a range model fitted to your own range test or sentinel tags is
the intended input. This page shows the stand-in, a model fitted with receiver depth, and a
model that also changes with date, read into a detection field for each day. It ends with the
array's coverage per day and what a silent receiver does to a surface.

## The stand-in: two distances

`de_logistic()` takes `d50` and `d05`, the distances at which half and 5% of transmissions
are heard, at one or more receiver depths, and interpolates them linearly between depths. The
Stoney example's range model is three lines:

```{r stand-in}
# Attach detfield, and ggplot2 for the figures
library(detfield)
library(ggplot2)
# Build the curve from d50 and d05 at 1 m and 35 m, with no spread
stand_in <- de_model(de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),
                                 depth = c(1, 35)),
                     sigma = list(station_hour = 0))
stand_in
```

`plot()` draws a detection model at the depths asked for:

```{r plot-stand-in, fig.height = 3.4, fig.alt = "The stand-in curve at receiver depths of 1, 10 and 25 m: detection probability falls with distance, more slowly at greater depth."}
# Draw the curve at three receiver depths
plot(stand_in, depth = c(1, 10, 25))
```

*The stand-in curve at three receiver depths.*

The stand-in is a guess at the shape. Use it to score a design before a range test, or to
see how a result changes with the curve; for positions, fit the curve to your study.

## A model fitted with depth

`stoney_range_test` is a range test at receiver depths of 1 m and 25 m, already counted by
`range_test_counts()`: one row per receiver, tag and hour, with the transmissions sent and
heard. A logistic regression on distance, depth and their interaction lets a deeper receiver
hear further; `de_model()` reads it as fitted:

```{r depth-model}
# Fit heard out of sent on distance, receiver depth and their interaction
depth_fit <- glm(cbind(heard, sent - heard) ~ distance_m * depth_m,
                 family = binomial, data = stoney_range_test)
depth_model <- de_model(depth_fit, sigma = list(station_hour = 0))
# Compare it with the stand-in at 250 m and 500 m, at 1 m and 25 m depth
check <- expand.grid(distance_m = c(250, 500), depth_m = c(1, 25))
check$fitted <- plogis(depth_model$predict(check$distance_m,
                                           depth_m = check$depth_m))
check$stand_in <- plogis(stand_in$predict(check$distance_m,
                                          depth_m = check$depth_m))
round(check, 3)
```

The range test was simulated from the stand-in's curve, so the two agree at the tested depths.
[Get started](detfield.html) fits the same model from the range-test files and draws it over
the counts.

## A model that changes with date

`stoney_range_covariates` is a range test of six days from 22 May 2024: three receivers at 1 m
and three at 25 m, each hearing eight tags of two models every hour. Its counts vary with the
day's wind, and between receivers and between hours. A sentinel test that runs through a
study gives this kind of record. The model takes a day number, and a level for each receiver
and hour for the random effect of a receiver-hour:

```{r prepare}
# Number the days from the first day of the test
range_test <- stoney_range_covariates
first_day <- as.Date("2024-05-22")
range_test$day <- as.numeric(as.Date(range_test$datetime) - first_day)
# Make factors for the receiver and receiver-hour random effects
range_test$receiver_hour <- factor(paste(range_test$receiver_serial,
                                         format(range_test$datetime)))
range_test$receiver_serial <- factor(range_test$receiver_serial)
range_test$tag_model <- factor(range_test$tag_model)
c(rows = nrow(range_test), days = length(unique(range_test$day)),
  receiver_hours = nlevels(range_test$receiver_hour))
```

`mgcv::bam()` fits the counts on distance, depth and their interaction, tag model, a smooth over
the day, and random effects for each receiver and each receiver-hour:

```{r fit-time}
# Fit a binomial GAM with a smooth over day and two random effects
time_fit <- mgcv::bam(
  cbind(heard, sent - heard) ~ distance_m * depth_m + tag_model +
    s(day, k = 5) + s(receiver_serial, bs = "re") +
    s(receiver_hour, bs = "re"),
  family = binomial, data = range_test, discrete = TRUE
)
summary(time_fit)$s.table
```


The counts were simulated with a fall of 0.25 logits for
each m/s of the day's mean wind (`?stoney_range_covariates`), so the smooth can be checked
against the day effect it should find:

```{r check-day}
# Predict the curve's logit at 300 m and 1 m depth for a V13-1x tag, each day
days <- data.frame(day = 0:5, distance_m = 300, depth_m = 1,
                   tag_model = "V13-1x",
                   receiver_serial = levels(range_test$receiver_serial)[1],
                   receiver_hour = levels(range_test$receiver_hour)[1])
fitted_logit <- predict(time_fit, days,
                        exclude = c("s(receiver_serial)", "s(receiver_hour)"))
# Set the day effect the counts were simulated with, from the day's wind
wind <- tapply(range_test$wind_ms, range_test$day, unique)
simulated_logit <- -0.25 * (wind - 4)
# Centre both on their mean and compare
round(data.frame(day = 0:5, wind_ms = wind,
                 fitted = fitted_logit - mean(fitted_logit),
                 simulated = simulated_logit - mean(simulated_logit)), 2)
```

The smooth finds the calm first day and the drop after it, and damps the day-to-day swings
that followed: a smooth over six days cannot follow a covariate that jumps between days. When
a weather record gives the driver, the day's wind can enter the model as a term instead, and a
smooth over date suits a sentinel record that runs for weeks or months. The spread the surfaces need is the standard deviation of
one receiver's hourly logit about the curve, here from the two random effects together:

```{r spread}
# Take the standard deviation of each random effect: for a binomial model
# its variance is 1 over the effect's smoothing parameter
sds <- 1 / sqrt(time_fit$sp[c("s(receiver_serial)", "s(receiver_hour)")])
round(sds, 2)
spread <- sqrt(sum(sds^2))
spread
```

`de_model()` reads the fit through `predict()` with the
random effects left out. A modulator gives the model each day's covariates: here a function
that turns a date into the day number. A covariates function adds the columns `predict()`
needs for the two left-out effects:

```{r time-model}
# Turn a date into the day number the smooth was fitted on
day_of <- function(date) as.numeric(as.Date(date) - first_day)
# Add a receiver and a receiver-hour level, which exclude = leaves out
add_levels <- function(pairs) {
  pairs$receiver_serial <- levels(range_test$receiver_serial)[1]
  pairs$receiver_hour <- levels(range_test$receiver_hour)[1]
  pairs
}
time_model <- de_model(time_fit, sigma = list(station_hour = spread),
                       modulators = list(day = day_of),
                       covariates = add_levels,
                       exclude = c("s(receiver_serial)", "s(receiver_hour)"))
time_model
```

For a fitted model given with a covariates function, `reads` lists only `distance_m`
(`?de_model`); the model still reads the receiver depth, the tag model and the day.
`de_field()` evaluates the
modulators for its `date` and reads the model at each receiver's depth. It needs the lake and the distances through water from the receivers, here the 70 of
the Stoney example:

```{r distances}
# Read the lake and measure distances through water from the receivers
lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "detfield"))
receivers <- stoney_track$receivers
distances <- water_distances(lake, receivers)
```

The receivers hear less of the lake on the windiest day of the test than on the calmest, here
for a V13-1x tag:

```{r time-fields}
# Build one field per day, for a V13-1x tag
field_days <- as.Date(c("2024-05-22", "2024-05-24"))
day_fields <- lapply(field_days, function(date) {
  suppressMessages(de_field(distances, time_model, tag_model = "V13-1x",
                            date = date))
})
# Share of water cells at least one receiver hears at 0.5 or more, per day
any_receiver <- lapply(day_fields, function(field) {
  1 - apply(1 - field$p, 1, prod)
})
round(vapply(any_receiver, function(p) mean(p >= 0.5), 0), 3)
```

```{r plot-time-fields, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 110, fig.alt = "Two maps of Stoney Lake side by side: the probability that any receiver detects a transmission on a calm day (left) and a windy day (right); the bright areas round the receivers are smaller on the windy day."}
# Put both days' probabilities in one table, one panel per day
panels <- paste0(c("(a) ", "(b) "), format(field_days, "%e %B"), ", wind ",
                 wind[c("0", "2")], " m/s")
day_cells <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(field, p, panel) {
  data.frame(terra::xyFromCell(lake, field$cells), p = p, panel = panel)
}, day_fields, any_receiver, panels))
day_cells$panel <- factor(day_cells$panel, panels)
# Map both, with the receivers
ggplot(day_cells, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = p)) +
  scale_fill_probability(name = "Detection\nprobability") +
  layer_receivers(receivers, size = 0.9, stroke = 0.35) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  annotation_scale_bar(location = "br", text_size = 2.4) +
  theme_positionr()
```

*Probability that at least one of the 70 Stoney receivers (rings) detects one
transmission of a V13-1x tag from each 100 m water cell, from the fitted model on (a) the
calmest and (b) the windiest day of the range test.*

`r percent(mean(any_receiver[[1]] >= 0.5))` of the water is heard at 0.5 or
more on the calm day and `r percent(mean(any_receiver[[2]] >= 0.5))` on the
windy one. Give `location_surface()` the counts of each day with the field of that day.

A modulator changes with the date and nothing finer, so a field varies by day and by
receiver and is constant within a day. Variation within a day, from hour to hour and receiver to receiver, is
the spread, `sigma$station_hour`, which the surfaces integrate over. A smooth over date
predicts only inside the dates its range test covered: run the sentinel tags through the
study, or model the covariate that drives range.

## Coverage per day

`system_de()` gives, for each water cell and day, the probability that at least `k` listening
receivers detect one transmission from it, from a table of which receivers listened on which
day. The rest of this page uses the stand-in, the curve the Stoney detections were drawn from.
Suppose one receiver, S034, was lost on the second day of the study:

```{r listening}
# Build the field of the stand-in curve
field <- de_field(distances, stand_in)
# Mark all 70 receivers listening on 1 June, and all but S034 on 2 June
stations <- receivers$station_id
listening <- data.frame(
  station_id = c(stations, setdiff(stations, "S034")),
  date = as.Date(rep(c("2024-06-01", "2024-06-02"),
                     c(length(stations), length(stations) - 1)))
)
table(listening$date)
```

```{r coverage}
# Compute coverage by at least one, and at least two, listening receivers
cover_1 <- system_de(field, listening, k = 1)
cover_2 <- system_de(field, listening, k = 2)
# Share of water cells at 0.5 or more, per day
daily_shares <- data.frame(
  date = sort(unique(listening$date)),
  heard_by_one = tapply(cover_1$p >= 0.5, cover_1$date, mean),
  heard_by_two = tapply(cover_2$p >= 0.5, cover_2$date, mean)
)
daily_shares
```

No cell is heard at 0.5 by two receivers on either day: under this curve one transmission is
placed by one receiver at most, so a position comes from the hourly counts of many
transmissions.

```{r coverage-map-data}
# Give each day's coverage its coordinates and a panel label
day_titles <- c("(a) 1 June, all receivers", "(b) 2 June, S034 not listening")
cover_1 <- cbind(cover_1, terra::xyFromCell(lake, cover_1$cell))
cover_1$panel <- factor(day_titles[match(cover_1$date,
                                         sort(unique(cover_1$date)))],
                        day_titles)
# Set a 4 km window round S034, and mark it on the second day
s034 <- receivers[receivers$station_id == "S034", ]
view <- list(x = s034$x + c(-2200, 2200), y = s034$y + c(-2200, 2000))
lost <- data.frame(s034[c("x", "y")], panel = factor(day_titles[2],
                                                     day_titles))
nrow(cover_1)
```

```{r coverage-map, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Two maps of the middle of Stoney Lake: coverage with all receivers on 1 June, and on 2 June with one receiver lost, which leaves a dark patch where it stood."}
# Map the coverage, the listening receivers and a cross at S034 on day two
ggplot(cover_1, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = p)) +
  scale_fill_probability(name = "Detection\nprobability") +
  layer_receivers(receivers[receivers$station_id != "S034", ], size = 2) +
  layer_receivers(transform(s034, panel = factor(day_titles[1], day_titles)),
                  size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = lost, shape = 4, colour = "#1A1A1A", size = 3,
             stroke = 2.4) +
  geom_point(data = lost, shape = 4, colour = "#FDE725", size = 3,
             stroke = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1) +
  coord_equal(xlim = view$x, ylim = view$y) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m, UTM 17N)", y = "Northing (m, UTM 17N)") +
  annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +
  theme_positionr()
```

*Probability that at least one listening receiver (rings) detects one transmission from
each 100 m water cell round station S034, under the stand-in curve, with all 70 receivers on 1
June (a). On 2 June (b) S034 (cross) is not listening.*

The loss leaves a dark patch where S034 stood, and the neighbours' ranges do not close it;
over the whole lake the share heard by one receiver at 0.5 falls from
`r percent(daily_shares$heard_by_one[1])` to `r percent(daily_shares$heard_by_one[2])`.
`system_de(format = "raster")` returns the same coverage as one raster layer per day.

## What a silent receiver does

A receiver that was listening and heard nothing is evidence: the animal was probably not near
it, and `bin_detections()` keeps it with `y = 0`. A receiver that was not listening is no
evidence, and must be left out of the listening table for those days, or its silence is read
as the first kind. The test case is the animal-hour in which one receiver logged the most
detections. Its surface is computed three ways: as logged, with that receiver's detections
lost but the receiver still marked listening, and with the receiver left out.

```{r silent-hour}
# Count the detections of the example study per animal, hour and receiver
counts <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, receivers,
                         stoney_track$tags)
# Find the busiest receiver-hour, and the counts of that animal-hour
busiest <- counts[which.max(counts$y), ]
as_logged <- counts[counts$animal_id == busiest$animal_id &
                      counts$bin_start == busiest$bin_start, ]
as_logged[as_logged$y > 0, c("animal_id", "bin_start", "station_id", "y", "n")]
```

```{r silent-cases}
# Set the busiest receiver's count to 0, still marked listening
silent_by_mistake <- as_logged
silent_by_mistake$y[silent_by_mistake$station_id == busiest$station_id] <- 0L
# Leave the busiest receiver out of the hour
left_out <- as_logged[as_logged$station_id != busiest$station_id, ]
hour_versions <- list(as_logged = as_logged,
                      silent_by_mistake = silent_by_mistake,
                      left_out = left_out)
```

Each version is scored by its 95% region's area and by the animal's true minutes in the hour
that the region holds:

```{r silent-receiver}
# Find the cells of the animal's true positions in the hour
track <- stoney_track$track
in_hour <- track$animal_id == busiest$animal_id &
  track$datetime >= busiest$bin_start &
  track$datetime < busiest$bin_start + 3600
true_cells <- terra::cellFromXY(lake, as.matrix(track[in_hour, c("x", "y")]))
# Compute each version's surface and 95% region, and score it
silent_scores <- t(vapply(hour_versions, function(hour_counts) {
  region <- credible_region(location_surface(hour_counts, field))
  c(region_ha = attr(region, "summary")$area_m2 / 1e4,
    minutes_inside = sum(true_cells %in% region$cell),
    minutes = length(true_cells))
}, numeric(3)))
silent_scores
```

As logged, the region holds `r silent_scores["as_logged", "minutes_inside"]` of the
`r length(true_cells)` minutes. With `r busiest$station_id` silent by mistake, the surface pushes
the animal away from the receiver that heard it most, and the region holds
`r silent_scores["silent_by_mistake", "minutes_inside"]`. Left out, the receiver adds nothing,
the other receivers place the animal, and the region holds
`r silent_scores["left_out", "minutes_inside"]` minutes over
`r silent_scores["left_out", "region_ha"]` ha. The
[**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/) R package marks the receiver-days on
which a receiver was not listening (`detqc::audit_listening()`), and `bin_detections()` reads
that table.
